note: Both sets are accurate and well-quoted, but Set B captures two additional supported facts — the flat-plate solar thermal collector's primary function of producing hot water and the passive design strategies used for the thermal envelope — that Set A omits. Set B also binds the supplemental electric-coil heat to the solar thermal collector (the component the sentence actually describes), whereas Set A loosely attributes it to HARVEST HOME as a whole. Neither set invents values or misreads the text, so the difference is coverage and binding precision.
remarks: Both sets miss the quantified fact that residential lighting consumed about 22% of a household's electrical use in California as of 2010 (with its citation), and both omit the Daylight Harvesting description and the two lighting system categories (main overhead vs. task lighting) in section 4.2. Set A's 'hot water supplemental heat source' claim is bound to HARVEST HOME rather than the solar thermal collector/hot water system — loose but not clearly wrong. The referenced diagram of desired light levels and equivalent incandescent bulb power is not present in the page image, so no claims can be drawn from it.
